facts.statement: The researchers used single-nucleus RNA sequencing to analyze 3.9 million nuclei taken from 178 adult human brain donors.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Individuals who had higher numbers of astrocytes, microglia, or oligodendrocyte precursor cells in one area of the brain generally showed the same increase in all other gray-matter regions studied.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The proportion of oligodendrocyte precursor cells dropped by 40% between the ages of 30 and 80 in both the cortex and the striatum.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Changes in gene expression linked to aging varied significantly depending on the specific type of cell being examined.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The study could estimate the age of brain donors based on their RNA expression patterns with an average error of 6.6 years.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Common genetic variations were linked to the expression of nearly 10,000 genes, and these links were mostly specific to cell types and helped distinguish neurons in the striatum from those in the cortex.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The authors state that the released data serve as a foundation for future research into human brain variation and potential vulnerabilities.
facts.subject: humans
